blocks.text: Sullivan Heights Condos and Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: Sullivan Heights sits inside the Lougheed Town Centre area, one of four Town Centres in Burnaby.
The City's Heritage Burnaby record places the Sullivan Heights subdivision east of Stoney Creek Park, with higher-density multi-family buildings west of the park.
The area is in the City of Burnaby, in School District 41's Cariboo Lougheed zone for trustee liaison purposes.

blocks.text: Sullivan Heights Condos and Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: The oldest part of the stock is the 1950s subdivision east of Stoney Creek Park, and the condo and townhome stock is mainly the multi-family building form west of the park, developed after 1974.

blocks.text: Sullivan Heights Condos and Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: A buyer planning an addition or redevelopment within 30 metres of a stream should expect a streamside leave area of 15 to 30 metres for a Class A fish-bearing watercourse, set by the Planning Department for the specific site.
The City's Environmental Review Committee can consider relaxing a streamside setback where full protection is not feasible, for a stated application fee.

blocks.text: Sullivan Heights Condos and Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The replacement Cameron Community Centre and Library is the main civic change here, and the City states it will be four times larger than the original 1988 facility.
The City provides weekly collection of recyclables for apartments, condos and townhomes, and a building must arrange City service through the Solid Waste and Recycling Division.
Green bin food scraps and yard waste are collected weekly from condos, apartments and townhomes as well as houses.
Burnaby Mountain Secondary is at 8800 Eastlake Drive, the secondary school listed by the Province for this district zone.

blocks.text: Sullivan Heights Condos and Townhomes: development and new projects

items.t: Cameron Community Centre and Library replacement, Lougheed Town Centre: under construction, estimated completion 2028, with an aquatic facility, expanded library, gym, fitness studios, indoor running track and civic plaza, per the City. Status read 2026-11-03.

Lougheed Village redevelopment (Starlight): the developer states the plan retains four existing rental buildings with 528 homes and adds 1,467 new rental homes for 1,995 total, near Lougheed Town Centre Station, with the rezoning application under City review on the developer's timeline page. Status read 2026-11-03.

blocks.text: Sullivan Heights Condos and Townhomes: costs and taxes

items.t: The strata-specific cost here is the flat sewer charge: Burnaby's 2025 fees bylaw sets a strata lot (not part of a duplex) at $399.95 if paid by March 17, 2025 and $421.00 after that date.
The same bylaw sets multiple-family dwellings, including townhouses and apartments, strata and non-strata, per unit, at the same $399.95 discounted and $421.00 full amounts for 2025.
The City's 2025 financial plan shows a sewer parcel tax of $739 for 2025 for an average single-family dwelling, billed with the February utility bill.

blocks.text: Sullivan Heights Condos and Townhomes: getting around

items.t: Lougheed Town Centre Station is the rapid-transit anchor, listed by TransLink as a transfer point between the Expo Line and the Millennium Line.
The Millennium Line, as TransLink describes it, takes riders from East Vancouver through Burnaby into Port Moody and Coquitlam.
The Expo Line, as TransLink describes it, connects downtown Vancouver with Burnaby, New Westminster and Surrey.

blocks.text: Sullivan Heights Condos and Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the streamside layer first: Burnaby's guide states the City has over 140 kilometres of open streams and that leave areas apply within 30 metres of a stream or freshwater wetland or shoreline.
The guide states the exact leave area for a specific site is determined by the Planning Department, so the map alone does not tell a buyer the final setback.
The City's Environmental Review Committee page is where a buyer checks how a setback relaxation application works and what it costs.

blocks.text: Sullivan Heights home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

97 condos sold in Sullivan Heights with a median price of $567,500 (the middle half sold between $503,000 and $685,000), taking a median of 29 days to sell at 97.4% of the last list price; 3% sold above list. They had a median $818 per square foot, a median year built of 2017 and a median strata fee of $449 a month. 8 townhomes sold in Sullivan Heights with a median price of $1,044,000 (the middle half sold between $782,750 and $1,096,500), taking a median of 40 days to sell at 97.5% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $756 per square foot, a median year built of 2004 and a median strata fee of $434 a month.
